title: Never really thought I would be a huge opera fan- but I’ve kind of be...
transcript: What if I told you that the most extravagant theater in New York is not happening on Broadway? In fact, it's not even close. I recently got to see my first show at the Metropolitan Opera House, and let me tell you, at least in terms of just pure scale, it blows anything on Broadway out of the water. We're talking hundreds of people on stage at a given time, giant, extravagant set pieces and costumes. They also have a massive orchestra. I'm talking, like, 100 musicians. It's also just like the most beautiful building you've ever seen in your life. The entire evening just feels so grand from start to finish. To give you a sense of the scale that they're able to work with, we actually got a chance to go backstage and speak with the technical director of the met, and he explained that the stage itself is actually only, like, one sixth of the total backstage area. That means for as big as the stage is, they have that amount of space on either side as well as behind. This allows them to have giant, fully built sets that they can just slide on and off. For comparison, I don't know if you've ever seen the wing space at a Broadway theater, but it is always incredibly tight. So much so that they'll actually have to hang set pieces from the ceiling because otherwise they don't have space for it. So having this massive wing space just Gives them a ton more options in terms of what they're able to do scenically. And so I honestly believe that seeing a show at the met, that is something every single person, whether you like opera or not, should do at least once in their life. Because you are not going to see theater at this scale, at this level of opulence, anywhere else.
